summary: Tiles tied to their own position in the scroll area: opacity, rise and scale advance exactly as far as the tile has entered, in both directions, with no JavaScript when the browser supports view timelines.
use: Scroll-driven entrances that must scrub with the finger (and reverse) instead of firing once: metric grids, feature lists, timelines.
spec: `MotionStage` from `@codeatlasdev/ui` with `loop={4600}`: autoplay scrolls the container, a wheel or touch scroll takes over
CSS `animation-timeline: view(block)` with `animation-range: entry 0% entry 70%` inside `@supports (animation-timeline: view())`
Keyframes `view-in`: `from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(28px) scale(0.92); }` to opacity 1, no translate, scale 1
Fallback without support: a `scroll` listener writes each tile's progress to `--v`, which drives the same opacity and transform
Under reduced motion `.vt--final` shows every tile settled and no listener is attached
